name: POST /api/empi/candidate-links/:link_id/steward-review - queue for steward
description: Queues a candidate link for human steward adjudication by opening an approval step on the given route_id; the steward identity is taken from the JWT (primary_persona_id, falling back to sub), never from the body. tenant_id falls back to the JWT tenant claim when the body omits it. Edge cases: a missing route_id, or no tenant_id in either the body or the token, -> 400; a candidate link that does not exist throws 'empi: candidate link <id> not found' inside the service and surfaces as a 500 InternalError with that message in details, NOT a 404 - this is the single most misleading status on the route; re-queuing an already-queued link opens a second approval step, so the endpoint is not idempotent; a token with no persona claim yields an empty steward_persona_id rather than an error.

errorCases.when: Authorization header absent or not in the form "Bearer <jwt>"
JWT signature invalid, malformed, or past its exp claim
body.route_id is missing, or tenant_id is absent from both the body and the JWT tenant claim
the link_id in the path matches no candidate-link row — surfaced as a 500 (with the message in details), not a 404
the approval-step insert or any other service call throws

testCases.name: Queue a candidate link for steward review

skipReason: TENANT-ISOLATION LIMIT, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param. Candidate links are raised only inside the probabilistic matcher (empiService.matchAndLink) — there is no HTTP write path that creates one — so the only reviewable link is a SEEDED fixture. The handler takes tenant_id from the JWT and deliberately NOT from the body (routes.ts: 'a body-supplied tenant would let a caller' cross the boundary), while this suite signs up a FRESH tenant on every run. The two fixtures therefore cannot both be true: empi_seed_candidate_link.sql stamps its link with the fixed tenant e22662dc-7e65-472a-a6da-41d59163714a, which a newly created tenant cannot see, and the older 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 row carries tenant_id NULL, which the tenant-scoped read excludes by construction — the seed's own comment says an unstamped fixture 'would be invisible to every caller'. Both were verified present in the local database and both are correctly invisible, which is why this returned 404 CandidateLinkNotFound rather than anything fixable in the definition. Making it auto needs either a stable QA tenant credential (none exists in test-config and no definition authenticates as a fixed tenant) or an HTTP route that raises a candidate link for the calling tenant. Covered meanwhile by seeding and calling it as the fixture tenant by hand. NOTE: {{var:link_id}} resolves to the tenant-NULL row, so it points at the one fixture that can never be returned; if a stable-tenant credential is ever added, repoint it at 0e3b1a70-0000-4000-8000-00000000e001 as well.
